scope: Proposition 5.1 (Universal action jump) of the manuscript “Uniqueness of tangent flows at the first singular time of embedded surface mean-curvature flow” (preprints/Tangent-flow-uniqueness-2026-09-24/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 355 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 19b2f77a4cbfb0d5), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 59-60. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let G+ and G− be the two array actions at a common parameter p in the inner parameter ball, and hence at common compact observation values, for a nonempty finite adverse end list with the same ordering of the bypasses on every end. Starting from these arrays, make the nonadverse synchronization (5.2) and use the single normalized preliminary solution stopped at Tpre above. Match Z∗,j from that solution by (5.4)–(5.7). The adverse continuations use the canonical profile gc and outgoing remainder derivatives ψ = ∂s(g − gc)|exit in the natural Neumann trace class (5.27), in the prescribed real path parameter at each exit. Let Y0 be the fixed large exit cutoff for this class. The continuation at the first fixed radius interpolates the preliminary circular derivative and that of gc as in Proposition 5.3. The longer shrinking branches have ψ = 0 at their own exits, and the shorter interpolation 60 OPENAI uses their actual remainder traces at the common shorter section. Proposition 5.3 proves membership in the relevant uniqueness balls and exact equality of the interpolation endpoints with the longer restrictions. For these actions there is a universal constant c ̸= 0 such that G+ − G− = c ∑ j adverse Z−2 ∗,j e−Z2 ∗,j/4 + o   ∑ j adverse |Z∗,j|−2 e−ℜZ2 ∗,j/4   . (5.11) With c0 defined by the upper-minus-lower y2 lateral labels in Lemma 5.6, c = ϵlab8πc0 for one common ϵlab ∈ {1, −1} determined by the array labels. Indeed an upper axial bypass in z2/Z2 0 becomes a lower r2 bypass under r2 = 2(1 − z2/Z2 0 ); this is one global label reversal, not an end-dependent sign. Reversing both array labels reverses c. More precisely, the limsup of the relative error as B → ∞ at fixed Y0 is bounded by a quantity tending to zero as Y0 → ∞.
